_comment: Two-channel colocalization tool. AutoForm over ColocViewModel. Left: a single-column Settings dock following the workflow order — pick a detector setup, load the image, pick the channel pair, set background/thresholds, then the optional gate and significance blocks. Right: tabbed views (coefficient table, both channel maps side by side, colocalized-pixel mask, intensity scatter whose rectangle ROI is the gate, van Steensel profile). Run / export live in the host toolbar; long help sits behind the ? button.

options.label: Setup
options.description: Detector setup whose named windows (green, red, …) become the pickable image channels — the same vocabulary as the rest of ChiSurf. Setups are created in the Detector Def tool. Leave it empty to use the raw detector channels stored in the file; it does not apply to camera images.

options.label: Image
options.description: The image to analyse: a TIFF stack (or any imageio-readable image), or a photon-stream file (PTU/HT3/…) reconstructed into a confocal-scan image — one channel per detector window of the setup above, or per raw routing channel when no setup is picked. Browse the disk, load a dataset registered in the database, or drop a file here.

sections.label: Channel A
sections.description: First channel of the pair. With a detector setup this lists its named windows (green, red, …); otherwise the channels found in the file (available after the first run).

sections.label: Channel B
sections.description: Second channel of the pair. Manders M1 answers 'how much of A sits with B', M2 the mirror question, so the A/B order matters for those two coefficients.

sections.label: Frame
sections.description: Which frame of the stack to analyse. -1 (default) sums every frame, which maximises the signal-to-noise of the coefficients; pick a single frame to follow a time series.

sections.label: Axis order
sections.description: Only for images whose axes are unlabelled. 'auto' treats a short leading axis (≤ 4 planes) as the channels and anything longer as frames; 'first axis' forces the leading axis to be the channels. TIFFs written with ImageJ/OME metadata are read exactly as labelled and ignore this.

sections.label: Auto background
sections.description: Estimate each channel's background as a low intensity quantile of that channel and subtract it. Background offsets bias Pearson and, much more strongly, Manders' overlap coefficient, so subtracting them is not optional for comparable numbers.

sections.label: Quantile
sections.description: Quantile used by the automatic background estimate. 0.05 (the lower 5 %) is the conventional choice: low enough to sit in dark/out-of-cell pixels, high enough not to be a single outlier.

sections.label: Background A
sections.description: Intensity subtracted from channel A before anything else. Filled in by the estimate; type your own value (e.g. a measured dark level) to override it.

sections.label: Background B
sections.description: Intensity subtracted from channel B before anything else.

sections.label: Costes thresholds
sections.description: Derive both thresholds from the data instead of by hand: an orthogonal regression of the channel pair is walked downwards until the pixels below it are no longer positively correlated. Everything below that point is indistinguishable from uncorrelated background. Hand-picked thresholds are the single largest source of irreproducible colocalization numbers.

sections.label: Threshold A
sections.description: A pixel counts as 'channel A present' above this background-subtracted intensity. Filled in by the Costes search when that is enabled.

sections.label: Threshold B
sections.description: A pixel counts as 'channel B present' above this background-subtracted intensity.

sections.label: Gate active
sections.description: Restrict the gated coefficients to a rectangle in the intensity-vs-intensity plane. Drag the blue rectangle on the 'Intensity scatter' tab to set it, or type the bounds below; the gated pixels are highlighted in the 'Colocalized pixels' map.

sections.label: A min
sections.description: Lower channel-A intensity of the gate rectangle.

sections.label: A max
sections.description: Upper channel-A intensity of the gate rectangle.

sections.label: B min
sections.description: Lower channel-B intensity of the gate rectangle.

sections.label: B max
sections.description: Upper channel-B intensity of the gate rectangle.

buttons.label: 🧹 Clear gate
buttons.description: Switch the gate off and recompute the coefficients over all thresholded pixels.

sections.label: Brush (px)
sections.description: Edge length of the square brush used to paint the region of interest on the Channel A map. Painting restricts every coefficient — thresholds, the null model and the profiles — to that region, the way a hand-drawn cell outline should.

buttons.label: 🧽 Clear ROI
buttons.description: Discard the painted region and analyse the whole image again.

sections.label: Object analysis
sections.description: Segment both channels into discrete particles and count how many coincide. This is the right question for puncta (vesicles, foci): on sparse spots the intensity coefficients are dominated by the empty background between them and report almost nothing.

sections.label: Tolerance (px)
sections.description: Centre-to-centre distance within which two objects count as coincident. Set it to the optical resolution — nothing can be localised better than the PSF, so demanding an identical centroid would only measure noise.

sections.label: Min size (px)
sections.description: Objects smaller than this are discarded as noise.

sections.label: Smoothing (σ px)
sections.description: Gaussian smoothing applied before segmenting; use it when shot noise fragments single objects into several.

sections.label: Split touching objects
sections.description: Separate objects that touch, with a distance-transform watershed. Helps dense puncta; over-segments irregular shapes.

sections.label: Costes randomization test
sections.description: Scramble one channel in PSF-sized blocks many times and compare the measured correlation against that null distribution. It answers the question the coefficients cannot: is this correlation more than what random co-occurrence of two dense stainings would give? Colocalization is conventionally called significant at p > 0.95. Costs one correlation per randomization.

sections.label: Block (px)
sections.description: Edge length of the scrambled blocks. Use the PSF width in pixels: smaller blocks destroy the image's own texture and make almost anything look significant, larger ones throw away resolution.

sections.label: Randomizations
sections.description: Size of the null distribution. 100–200 is enough for a p-value quoted to two decimals; more only sharpens the tail.

sections.label: Seed
sections.description: Seed of the random generator, so the same image and settings always give the same p-value (a reported number stays reproducible).

sections.label: van Steensel shift (px)
sections.description: Largest horizontal shift of the cross-correlation profile; 0 disables it. The profile peaks at 0 for true colocalization and away from 0 when the channels are misregistered — the standard check for chromatic aberration before trusting any coefficient.

sections.label: Profile bins
sections.description: Number of intensity bins in the 'PCC vs intensity' profiles. Fewer bins average more pixels per point (smaller error bars), more bins resolve where in the brightness range the correlation changes.

sections.label: Histogram bins
sections.description: Bins per axis of the intensity scatter (joint histogram). More bins resolve fine structure in the cloud; fewer make sparse images look continuous.

sections.label: Log histogram
sections.description: Show the intensity scatter on a logarithmic count scale, so the sparse bright tail stays visible next to the dense background cloud.

columns.label: Coefficient
columns.description: Colocalization coefficient (see the ? help for what each one answers).

columns.label: Value
columns.description: Computed value; 'n/a' when it is undefined for this selection (e.g. no pixel above threshold).

sections.title: Channel A
sections.description: Background-subtracted map of channel A. Paint on it to restrict the analysis to a region of interest.

sections.title: Channel B
sections.description: Background-subtracted map of channel B.

sections.title: Colocalized pixels
sections.description: Pixels above both thresholds; gated pixels are brighter when a scatter gate is active.

sections.title: Intensity scatter
sections.description: Joint histogram of the two channels (A horizontal, B vertical). Drag the blue rectangle to gate a pixel population.

sections.title: CCF map (2-D)
sections.description: Full 2-D cross-correlation plane: the peak sits at the (Δx, Δy) that realigns the channels, so a vertical registration offset is visible too.

sections.title: Objects
sections.description: Segmented objects: 1 = channel A only, 2 = channel B only, 3 = both — coincidence read directly off the map.
